cards.explanation: The answer is money, friends. The man was put at the Beautiful Gate every day to beg from the people going into the temple courts, so he asked Peter and John for money. I bet to him they were just two more folks walking in. I think he expected a few coins and a quiet afternoon.

The answer is True. The man gave them his attention, "…expecting to receive something from them." He had just asked for money, so I'd say his hand was already halfway out. Hold that thought, friends, because he's about to get something way bigger than a coin.

The answer is Jesus Christ of Nazareth. Peter says, "In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk!" He had no silver or gold, but he had that name. The power wasn't his own, and he points straight at Jesus.

The answer is False, friends. Peter helped him up, "…and at once the man’s feet and ankles were made strong." No slow recovery, no waiting for next week. The change was immediate, and the man was standing on his own two feet.

The answer is into the temple courts. The text says, "Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking and leaping and praising God." This man used to be set down outside the temple gate. Now he walks in on his own feet, and I think that's the best entrance anybody has ever made.

The answer is praising God. The text says he went in "…walking and leaping and praising God." His feet worked, and he was praising God right along with the walking and leaping. I think if I could leap like that, friends, I'd forget about my hat entirely.

The answer is the man who begged at the Beautiful Gate. The people "…recognized him as the man who used to sit begging at the Beautiful Gate of the temple…" That man had his spot at the gate, and now he was walking and praising God. Imagine seeing someone you know from one spot suddenly up and walking, friends.

The answer is True. The people "…were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him." They knew that he'd been begging at the gate, and now he was walking. I'd be amazed too, and I'd probably need a chair.

The answer is Solomon's, friends. Solomon was David's son and Israel's king (1 Kings 2:12), and a walkway at the temple carries his name: Solomon's Colonnade. The people ran there to Peter and John. It's a walkway, and I think it filled up fast.

The answer is False. Peter asks, "Why do you stare at us as if by our own power or godliness we had made this man walk?" He doesn't take the credit for himself. I love a man who hands the trophy back.

The answer is let Him go free, friends. Peter says the people handed Jesus over and rejected Him before Pilate, the Roman governor (Matthew 27:2), "…even though he had decided to release Him." Pilate had decided to let Him go, and the people still rejected Jesus. It's a heavy detail.

The answer is murderer. Peter says, "You rejected the Holy and Righteous One and asked that a murderer be released to you." It's a hard thing to hear, and I think Peter knows it. He puts the Holy and Righteous One right next to a murderer, and the difference is clear.

The answer is True, friends. Peter says, "You killed the Author of life, but God raised Him from the dead, and we are witnesses of this fact." The "we" includes Peter, so he stands as a witness. He isn't passing along a rumor.

The answer is faith. Peter says, "…the faith that comes through Him that has given him this complete healing in your presence." The man's healing is complete, and Peter ties it to Jesus' name and faith. He doesn't claim any of it for himself.

The answer is True. Peter says God "…has fulfilled what He foretold through all the prophets, saying that His Christ would suffer." He's telling the crowd that this wasn't a surprise to God. The prophets had already spoken about it.

The answer is wiped away, friends. Peter says, "Repent, then, and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away…" Think of wiping the counter clean after a big batch, except this is so much better. Turn back, and the sins are gone.

The answer is the restoration of all things. Peter says, "Heaven must take Him in until the time comes for the restoration of all things, which God announced long ago through His holy prophets." Jesus stays in heaven until then. I can't tell you when that day comes, friends, but I keep my ovens ready.

The answer is to listen to Him in everything He says. Peter quotes Moses, Israel's leader, who said, "You must listen to Him in everything He tells you." Everything, friends, not just the easy parts or the parts that fit your schedule. Peter brings this up to point the crowd to the prophet God would raise up.

The answer is False, friends. Peter says, "…all the prophets from Samuel on, as many as have spoken, have proclaimed these days." Samuel was a prophet of the LORD (1 Samuel 3:20). Moses was just one voice in a long line.

The answer is by turning each of them from their wicked ways. Peter says God sent His Servant "…to bless you by turning each of you from your wicked ways." That's the blessing, friends, and it's for each one of them. Peter had told the man at the gate that he had no silver or gold, and this is better than both.
